text: Grandparents had cheap needs and expensive wants. Today it's the reverse.
Black Friday: 30% off. January: 100% of it is due.

A $65,000 salary sounds like $31.25 an hour.

Now do the REAL math.

After federal tax and FICA: $54,408.
That's $26.16 an hour.

Now add the hours the job takes that nobody pays for:

• Commute (27 min each way): 225 hours a year
• Getting ready: 125 hours
• Unpaid lunch break: 125 hours
• "Quick" emails after hours: 100 hours

That's 2,655 hours a year, not 2,080.

Now subtract what it costs just to show up:

• Gas for the commute: $1,250
• Lunches out twice a week: $1,500
• Work clothes: $500

What's actually left: $51,158.

Divided by 2,655 hours?

$19.27 an hour.

$31.25 quietly became $19.27.

That's why a $58,000 remote job can pay MORE per hour of your life than a $65,000 office job.

Nobody puts that number in the job posting.

Buy now, pay later is about to have its biggest month of the year.

38% of holiday shoppers plan to use it this season.

And 38% of THOSE shoppers already expect to miss a payment.

Here's the math nobody does at checkout:

• Black Friday TV: $400 = 4 payments of $100
• Cyber Monday shoes: $160 = 4 payments of $40
• Gifts for the family: $600 = 4 payments of $150

That's $290 due every two weeks, with the last round landing in January.

Right next to rent. Right next to the December credit card bill.

All for stuff that's already been unwrapped.

A deal is only a deal if it's paid off when the box shows up.
